name: Tesla
intro: Tesla is an American electric-car brand. Start with two names you may often hear together: Model 3 is a lower sedan and Model Y is a taller crossover. Then learn Model S, Model X and Cybertruck as different product families. This track adds charging, version names and practical comparisons, rather than treating every Tesla as the same car.
naming: Model 3 and Model Y are family names, not the number of electric motors. Rear-Wheel Drive describes driven wheels. Dual Motor means two motors on that specified version; it does not mean two petrol engines. Long Range and Performance are version names whose specification and availability change. Software features and physical vehicle hardware are separate parts of a purchase.
warning: The course includes selected Canadian families plus explicitly labelled older/current road-recognition examples. Check the exact year, body, engine/drive configuration and current availability before using specifications or prices. The families below are selected for learning and recognition. Check the linked official range for current Canadian availability, model years, equipment and pricing. A familiar name may remain on used cars after new-car availability changes.

models.name: Model 3
models.explanation: Model 3 is Tesla’s electric sedan family. It has a lower car body and separate trunk opening, distinct from the taller Model Y crossover.
models.tradeoff: The Model 3 belongs in a comparison for tesla everyday electric sedan. Check actual passenger fit, cargo access, exterior dimensions and the exact version’s running costs. Its category is a starting point, not a promise that it fits every person or task.
models.compare: Compare Model 3 with Model Y on passenger access and cargo shape, then compare the exact battery/drive versions, price and charging needs.
models.scenario: Mina commutes alone, carries ordinary bags and likes a lower seating position. A Model 3 belongs on her comparison list. If she starts carrying a tall, rigid box, she should test the trunk opening rather than assume a more powerful version solves that loading problem.
models.power: Model 3 is battery-electric: there is no petrol engine, engine displacement or combustion-cylinder count. Rear-wheel-drive and all-wheel-drive versions are distinct configurations in relevant years. Compare the actual battery/range, wheels and equipment rather than assigning one specification to every Model 3.

knowledgeCheck.prompt: A Model 3 listing says Dual Motor. What does that describe?
knowledgeCheck.correct: Two electric drive motors
wrong: A two-cylinder petrol engine
Two fuel tanks
Two passenger seats
knowledgeCheck.why: Motor count describes electric propulsion. It is separate from the model-family name and seating capacity.

practicalDetails: The separate trunk opening is the first practical distinction to learn against Model Y. A car can have useful luggage volume but an opening that will not admit a tall box. Opening shape and total volume answer different questions; try the actual object rather than comparing only a litre figure.

A lower seating position may appeal to one driver and make entry/exit less comfortable for another. That is a fit preference, not a universal quality score. Compare the view, getting in and out, rear-passenger access and your parking space before choosing a battery or performance version.

Once the body suits you, compare similar model years and equipment. A faster Model 3 version can change the power/drive specification without changing a sedan into an SUV. The charging routine and exact range/efficiency information need the actual version, not just “a Tesla.”

models.name: Model Y
models.explanation: Model Y is Tesla’s electric crossover family. The taller body and lifting rear hatch create a different practical role from Model 3.
models.tradeoff: The Model Y belongs in a comparison for tesla family crossover. Check actual passenger fit, cargo access, exterior dimensions and the exact version’s running costs. Its category is a starting point, not a promise that it fits every person or task.
models.compare: Check actual seating configuration and cargo space; do not assume every year and version has identical capacity. Compare charging and trip needs for the exact version.
models.scenario: Arun and his partner regularly carry passengers and a bulky stroller. Their Model Y-versus-Model 3 comparison starts with rear access, the actual loading opening and space while passengers are seated. They can compare battery/drive versions after those must-haves are met.
models.power: Model Y is battery-electric. A version can differ in driven wheels, battery/range, wheels and seating configuration. A facelift means a visual/equipment update; it does not turn every older Model Y into the updated car. Use Canadian specifications for the exact version.

knowledgeCheck.prompt: A Model Y listing says Dual Motor. What should you understand?
knowledgeCheck.correct: It has two electric drive motors; check the full version
wrong: It must use a petrol range-extender
Its battery capacity must be exactly double a RWD version
Its range is fixed in every weather condition
knowledgeCheck.why: Dual Motor describes motor count. It does not by itself settle battery capacity, exact range or the full model-year configuration.

practicalDetails: Model Y’s rear hatch lifts with the rear window. That gives it a different loading opening from Model 3’s separate trunk lid. To compare usefulness, test the object you carry with the rear seats in the position you need; cargo space measured with seats folded does not describe a trip with people sitting there.

The taller crossover layout can change the feeling of getting in, sitting and seeing out. Try it with the people who actually travel in the car. A high seat is not proof of a universal safety advantage, and an SUV name does not settle adult rear-seat comfort.

Do not assume every Model Y has the same seat count, drive system or battery. A listing needs its year and configuration. A performance version does not create a missing seating row or a different rear-door opening, and a software update cannot add those physical features.

models.name: Model S & Model X
models.explanation: Model S is a larger electric car family; Model X is an SUV family. These names remain useful for road and used-car recognition even if new-car availability changes.
models.tradeoff: The Model S & Model X belongs in a comparison for tesla’s larger electric families. Check actual passenger fit, cargo access, exterior dimensions and the exact version’s running costs. Its category is a starting point, not a promise that it fits every person or task.
models.compare: Model X’s distinctive rear doors are a clue, not evidence of one particular battery or software configuration. Verify current availability and exact year/version before using a price.
models.scenario: A friend mentions a Model S & Model X. Explain its role as tesla’s larger electric families, then ask for the year, powertrain and equipment before comparing it with another Tesla.
models.power: Model S and Model X are different battery-electric families. Both can have version names such as Plaid, but a shared performance label does not make the sedan/liftback and SUV the same body. Earlier versions and current ordering availability need separate checks.

knowledgeCheck.prompt: What does Model S versus Model X primarily distinguish?
knowledgeCheck.correct: Different vehicle families and bodies
wrong: Only the paint colour
The number of petrol cylinders
A free software update
knowledgeCheck.why: Model S is the larger low car family; Model X is the SUV family. Version names add another layer.

models.name: Model S
models.explanation: Model S is Tesla’s larger low passenger-car family. Its liftback rear opening rises with the rear window, a useful distinction from the Model 3’s separate trunk opening. Larger and more expensive does not mean it is the right everyday car for every driver.
models.tradeoff: The liftback opening and larger-car role can matter for luggage and passengers, while its size, tires and running costs still need checking. An older used Model S can have very different hardware and charging capabilities from another year.
models.compare: Compare Model S with Model 3 for a different-size lower-car role and with Model X for SUV packaging. A used Model S at a similar asking price to a newer Model 3 still needs a condition, battery/warranty and total-cost comparison.
models.memory: S = larger low car with a liftback
models.scenario: A friend needs to load a wide box. Comparing the actual rear openings of Model 3 and Model S is more useful than comparing their acceleration figures.
models.power: Battery-electric propulsion. Plaid is a performance version name, not the definition of every Model S. Do not infer a version’s motor count or charging specification from an old review.

knowledgeCheck.prompt: Which opening helps distinguish Model S from Model 3?
knowledgeCheck.correct: Model S has a liftback that includes the rear window
wrong: Model S always has a pickup bed
Model 3 has no rear luggage space
Both names mean identical body panels
knowledgeCheck.why: Model S uses a liftback; Model 3 uses a separate rear trunk opening.

models.name: Model X
models.role: Tesla SUV known for its distinctive rear doors
models.explanation: Model X is Tesla’s larger SUV family, known for upward-opening Falcon Wing rear doors. These doors are a strong recognition clue, but they do not identify the year, battery, number of seats or exact version.
models.tradeoff: Try the actual seating arrangement and access with the passengers you carry. Distinctive door operation is something to test in the places you park, rather than assuming it works the same as an ordinary hinged rear door.
models.compare: Compare Model X with Model Y on exact seating, loading, dimensions and costs. Do not call Model X merely an expensive trim of Model Y: it is a separate family.
models.memory: X = SUV with Falcon Wing rear doors
models.scenario: Someone shows you a Tesla SUV with unusual upward-opening rear doors. You can identify the Model X family while still asking for the year and configuration.
models.power: Battery-electric. Seat counts and hardware vary across versions and years. A Plaid name describes a particular performance configuration, not all examples.

knowledgeCheck.prompt: What can the distinctive rear doors help you identify?
knowledgeCheck.correct: The Model X family, not its exact specification
wrong: The precise battery capacity on every year
A petrol engine under the bonnet
The owner’s software purchases
knowledgeCheck.why: A visual feature can identify the family while leaving version, year and equipment unresolved.

models.name: Cybertruck
models.explanation: Cybertruck is Tesla’s electric pickup family, with a very angular body and an open load-bed role. It is separate from the brand’s sedans and SUVs. This is also a recognition lesson: current ordering and production availability must be checked directly.
models.tradeoff: A pickup’s usefulness depends on the bed, load limits, exact configuration and intended job. A distinctive exterior is not a specification of towing ability or real-trip range. Size and access deserve a parking test.
models.compare: Compare Cybertruck with an exact electric or combustion pickup configuration on payload, towing needs, charging/fuelling, bed access and costs. A maximum tow figure and a maximum range figure may not describe the same loaded trip.
models.scenario: A friend wants to tow on a long trip. Ask for the trailer’s actual loaded requirements and the vehicle configuration, then plan the energy stops; do not choose from an unloaded range headline.
models.power: Battery-electric. Motors, rated capability and range depend on configuration. Towing and load change energy use; the route and charging access matter.

knowledgeCheck.prompt: Does an unloaded range figure guarantee the same towing range?
knowledgeCheck.correct: No — load, route and conditions change energy use
wrong: Yes, every trip uses identical energy
Only if the paint is uncoated
Yes, pickup beds remove drag
knowledgeCheck.why: Rated range is not a guarantee for a loaded towing trip.

workshops.title: Tesla: charging without the jargon
workshops.subtitle: kW, kWh, home charging, Superchargers and realistic trips.

pages.title: Energy and charging speed are different
pages.text: kWh (kilowatt-hours) is an amount of electrical energy. kW (kilowatts) is a rate: how quickly energy is being delivered or used. Think of kWh as the amount in a bucket and kW as how fast you fill it.
pages.example: Illustrative arithmetic: adding 20 kWh at a steady 10 kW would take two hours before allowing for losses or changes in charging speed. These are practice inputs, not a Tesla specification.
paragraphs: Energy amount and charging rate are different units. A large peak kW number is not a battery capacity.

pages.title: Make a charging routine, not just a range wish
pages.text: Home/work AC charging and road-trip DC fast charging solve different routines. A dependable place to recharge while parked can matter more than a headline peak speed. Building access and installation details need checking for your own situation.
pages.example: A condo resident has no assigned charger but can reliably charge at work. Assess that routine instead of assuming every owner can simply install a charger at home.
paragraphs: An EV ownership plan depends on practical charging access, not merely the existence of a charging port.

pages.title: A peak is not the whole session
pages.text: DC charging speed changes during a session with factors such as battery condition/state, temperature and charger capability. A peak rate cannot be multiplied across the entire charge and assumed constant. Range also changes with conditions and use.
pages.example: If a review quotes a peak, ask how long the relevant charge window took on that vehicle and under those conditions.
paragraphs: A charging curve varies; the highest point is not a promise of the average rate for an entire session.

pages.title: Plan the actual trip
pages.text: Identify the exact car/year, compatible connector, charging network and route. Use the vehicle’s route/charging guidance and verify site access. Loaded trips and cold conditions can change energy needs. You do not need to memorize one range number as a guarantee.
pages.example: A 300-km trip with a loaded car is a planning task: charging locations, access and conditions matter alongside the version’s rating.
paragraphs: Rated figures are comparison references, not a guarantee for every route, load and weather condition.

questions.prompt: Which unit describes an amount of stored electrical energy?
questions.why: Energy amount and charging rate are different units. A large peak kW number is not a battery capacity.

questions.prompt: What should come before relying on regular overnight charging?
options: Confirming dependable access where the car is parked
Assuming every condo has a charger
Using the model number as the socket type
Expecting a petrol engine as backup
questions.why: An EV ownership plan depends on practical charging access, not merely the existence of a charging port.

questions.prompt: Why can a peak fast-charge rate mislead as a whole-session estimate?
options: The charging rate changes during the session
The car always holds the peak until full
The vehicle has a petrol tank instead
questions.why: A charging curve varies; the highest point is not a promise of the average rate for an entire session.

questions.prompt: Does one advertised range number guarantee every trip distance?
options: No — version, use and conditions matter
Yes, ratings are promises in all weather
Yes, adding passengers never changes energy use
questions.why: Rated figures are comparison references, not a guarantee for every route, load and weather condition.

workshops.title: Tesla: versions, updates & used-car listings
workshops.subtitle: Separate the body, driven wheels, hardware and software.

pages.title: Model 3 versus Model Y
pages.text: Model 3 is the lower sedan family; Model Y is the taller crossover with a lifting rear hatch. Pick the body for passenger access and loading, then compare the particular battery/drive version.
pages.example: Try a bulky item through both actual rear openings instead of assuming the faster version has more luggage room.
paragraphs: Sedan and crossover packaging are a different decision from motor power or battery configuration.

pages.title: Version names need a year
pages.text: RWD describes driven wheels; Dual Motor identifies two electric motors on that specified product. Performance and Long Range are version names, not one permanent set of numbers across every generation and market.
pages.example: Two used listings can both say Long Range while having different years and hardware. Match the exact specification before using one review for both.
paragraphs: A version name is a starting label, not a timeless hardware specification.

pages.title: An update is not a new physical car
pages.text: A software update can change supported features. It does not physically add a different body opening, a missing seating row or a larger battery. Hardware and feature support need checking in the actual listing.
pages.example: A seller promises that a software update turns an older body into the redesigned generation. Ask exactly which software feature changes and which physical hardware remains.
paragraphs: Software changes do not create missing physical body, seat or battery hardware.

pages.title: Read assistance-feature names carefully
pages.text: FSD (Supervised) is a driver-assistance product requiring active supervision. The name does not turn the car into an autonomous vehicle. For a used listing, verify current feature eligibility and subscription/purchase terms directly.
pages.example: A friend assumes the feature name means they can stop supervising. Read Tesla’s current description and requirements rather than taking the name literally.
paragraphs: Tesla identifies the supervised product as requiring active driver supervision; the feature name is not autonomous-driving authorization.

options: Assuming both have identical rear openings
questions.why: Sedan and crossover packaging are a different decision from motor power or battery configuration.

questions.prompt: Does a Long Range name guarantee identical hardware across all years?
options: No — compare the actual year and configuration
It always means a petrol range extender
questions.why: A version name is a starting label, not a timeless hardware specification.

questions.prompt: Which change cannot happen purely through a software download?
options: Adding a physical extra seating row
questions.why: Software changes do not create missing physical body, seat or battery hardware.

questions.prompt: What does FSD (Supervised) still require?
options: A change to a petrol engine
questions.why: Tesla identifies the supervised product as requiring active driver supervision; the feature name is not autonomous-driving authorization.

name: Toyota
intro: Toyota is a Japanese brand with everyday cars, several SUV sizes, minivans, pickups and sports cars. Learn Corolla, Camry and RAV4 first, then place the neighbouring families around them. Hybrid describes how a car is powered; it does not describe its shape or passenger capacity.
naming: Corolla, Camry and RAV4 are families. LE, XLE, SE, XSE and Limited are version/equipment labels used differently across models. GR identifies particular performance products. Hybrid and Plug-in Hybrid are different systems; Prime is an older plug-in badge you may hear in conversation.
warning: The course includes selected Canadian families plus explicitly labelled older/current road-recognition examples. Check the exact year, body, engine/drive configuration and current availability before using specifications or prices. The families below are selected for learning and recognition. Check the linked official range for current Canadian availability, model years, equipment and pricing. A familiar name may remain on used cars after new-car availability changes.

models.name: Corolla
models.explanation: Corolla is Toyota’s compact passenger-car family, with sedan and hatchback forms depending on year and version. Corolla Cross is a separately named SUV family, not just the hatchback’s full name.
models.tradeoff: The Corolla belongs in a comparison for compact everyday toyota car. Check actual passenger fit, cargo access, exterior dimensions and the exact version’s running costs. Its category is a starting point, not a promise that it fits every person or task.
models.compare: Compare Corolla with Camry for different sedan roles; compare with Corolla Cross for an SUV body. GR Corolla is a distinct performance version, not an equipment package on every Corolla.
models.memory: Corolla = compact car; Cross = check the SUV
models.scenario: Sam wants a compact commuter and occasionally carries a large music case. Compare the actual sedan/hatch openings and rear-seat needs before moving to Corolla Cross or a higher equipment grade.
models.power: Corolla sedans have offered conventional gas and hybrid versions in Canada; hatchback and GR Corolla versions have different specifications. A conventional hybrid does not use an external charging routine. Check whether AWD is actually offered on the chosen year/body/powertrain.

knowledgeCheck.prompt: Does every Corolla body use the same hybrid drivetrain?
knowledgeCheck.correct: No — body, year and version need separate checks
wrong: Yes, all Corollas are plug-in hybrids
Yes, hatchback means AWD
Only the badge colour changes
knowledgeCheck.why: Sedan, hatchback, hybrid and GR products are different configurations.

practicalDetails: Sedan and hatchback are different loading arrangements: the sedan has a separate trunk lid, while a hatch opens with the rear window. A bulky object can fit one opening and not another even when quoted luggage volumes seem close.

Keep the four names separate in conversation: Corolla, Corolla Hatchback, Corolla Cross and GR Corolla. Cross changes the family/body role; GR identifies a distinct performance product. A trim word such as SE does not settle all of those differences.

models.name: Camry
models.explanation: Camry occupies a larger sedan role than Corolla. It is still a lower passenger car with a separate trunk, rather than a taller SUV. The same family name has continued across many generations.
models.tradeoff: The Camry belongs in a comparison for larger everyday toyota sedan. Check actual passenger fit, cargo access, exterior dimensions and the exact version’s running costs. Its category is a starting point, not a promise that it fits every person or task.
models.compare: Compare Camry with Corolla on actual space, comfort, efficiency and costs. Compare with RAV4 if the key question is sedan versus SUV.
models.scenario: Two friends both say they drive a Camry. One has an older gas example and one a newer hybrid. You can recognize the family while still needing each year and powertrain to compare their cars.
models.power: The 2026 Canadian Camry range uses hybrid power. Older Camrys on the road include different gas engines, so the family name alone cannot identify the system. A conventional hybrid recharges through its own operation rather than a household plug.

knowledgeCheck.prompt: A current Camry is a conventional hybrid. What charging routine should you expect?
knowledgeCheck.correct: No routine external plugging-in
wrong: A required DC fast-charge stop after every trip
Petrol is never used
The same battery-only routine as a Model 3
knowledgeCheck.why: A conventional hybrid combines a combustion engine with electric assistance without routine external charging.

practicalDetails: Camry and Corolla are different sedan families. Test adult rear-seat fit, the trunk opening and the exterior dimensions you must park; do not treat a higher Corolla equipment grade as the same thing as a different-size Camry body.
For an older used Camry, ask the year and exact engine before discussing fuel or cylinder count. A current hybrid-range description is not a specification for every Camry already on BC roads.

models.name: RAV4
models.explanation: RAV4 is Toyota’s compact SUV family. Its job is different from the Corolla sedan even if both are everyday household vehicles. A new generation can change which hybrid systems are offered.
models.tradeoff: The RAV4 belongs in a comparison for core toyota family suv. Check actual passenger fit, cargo access, exterior dimensions and the exact version’s running costs. Its category is a starting point, not a promise that it fits every person or task.
models.compare: Compare RAV4 with Corolla Cross for different SUV sizes and with Highlander/Grand Highlander for three-row needs. Do not confuse a regular hybrid with a plug-in version.
models.scenario: A family compares RAV4 and Highlander because grandparents sometimes join them. First check the actual passenger arrangement and bags; only then discuss which grade, engine/electric system and price fit.
models.power: Toyota’s Canadian 2026 RAV4 range is hybrid and plug-in hybrid; older gas-only RAV4s remain common recognition examples. The plug-in version has an externally rechargeable battery. Do not transfer an older engine specification to the redesigned model year.

knowledgeCheck.prompt: Which detail matters when discussing a 2026 Canadian RAV4?
knowledgeCheck.correct: Whether it is Hybrid or Plug-in Hybrid
wrong: Whether RAV4 means four electric motors
Whether every old RAV4 has the new drivetrain
Whether an XLE badge guarantees a charging port
knowledgeCheck.why: The new Canadian range distinguishes hybrid and plug-in systems; the model year matters.

practicalDetails: Start with whether a two-row family SUV meets the passenger and loading task. If more than five usable places are a real requirement, a higher equipment grade on a five-seat RAV4 cannot create a third row.

Then compare the exact energy system. A conventional hybrid and plug-in hybrid require different charging discussions. A household with reliable charging and one without it should not automatically make the same powertrain choice.

models.name: Corolla Cross
models.explanation: Corolla Cross is an SUV family, separate from Corolla sedan and hatchback. The shared Corolla name is a clue to its place in the everyday range, not proof of an identical body or powertrain.
models.tradeoff: Test its rear-seat and luggage fit against your needs. Smaller SUVs can be useful for access and parking, but an SUV label alone cannot establish that a large box fits better than in a hatchback.
models.compare: Compare Corolla Cross with RAV4 for different SUV sizes and with Corolla for a lower body. Ask whether the specific Cross is gas or hybrid.
models.memory: Cross = the SUV, not the Corolla hatchback
models.scenario: A friend says “Corolla,” but the photo shows a taller crossover. Ask whether they mean Corolla Cross before comparing it with a Civic.
models.power: Gas and hybrid configurations depend on year. A hybrid’s drive layout and equipment must be checked for that exact Canadian version.

models.name: Prius & Prius Plug-in Hybrid
models.explanation: Prius is a low liftback family associated with hybrid power. Prius Plug-in Hybrid, previously called Prius Prime in relevant years, adds an externally rechargeable battery. The similar body does not erase the difference.
models.tradeoff: A plug-in version can use charging for part of the routine, but only if charging fits the owner’s life. Check the exact cabin and luggage arrangement as well as energy use.
models.compare: Compare Prius with Corolla Hybrid for different passenger-car packaging, and compare Prius hybrid versus plug-in using charging access and actual price.
models.memory: Prius = liftback; Plug-in/Prime adds a charging question
models.scenario: Two neighbours have similar-looking Priuses, but only one plugs in. Identify the exact version instead of assuming one owner is using the car incorrectly.
models.power: Conventional hybrid and plug-in hybrid combine an engine and electric assistance in different ways. Neither is the same system as a battery-only Tesla.

models.name: Highlander
models.explanation: Highlander is a Toyota crossover family with a three-row role. It is distinct from RAV4 and from the separately named Grand Highlander. A third row must be judged with the required passengers and luggage in place.
models.tradeoff: Try access to the back row and see what space remains behind it. A nominal seat count does not tell you whether adults, child seats and bags work together for your trip.
models.compare: Compare Highlander with RAV4 when deciding whether a third row is needed, and with Grand Highlander or Sienna when rear-row use is frequent.
models.scenario: A driver occasionally carries grandparents and children together. Their checklist starts with access, fit and luggage, not a bigger engine badge.
models.power: Gas/hybrid availability depends on model year. A hybrid badge does not guarantee plug-in charging or a particular tow rating.

models.name: Grand Highlander
models.explanation: Grand Highlander is a separate Toyota family with a larger three-row role than Highlander. Grand is part of the model name, not a trim you can add to any Highlander.
models.tradeoff: Check the actual third-row fit and load space, then compare the larger exterior with the places you park. More room has a physical-size trade-off.
models.compare: Compare Grand Highlander with Highlander for passenger/cargo needs and with Sienna for minivan access and layout. Hybrid and Hybrid MAX versions are separate mechanical choices.
models.scenario: Your friend says their Highlander became a Grand Highlander by choosing a premium package. Explain that these are separate families.
models.power: Gas, conventional hybrid and Hybrid MAX configurations in relevant years have different performance and efficiency. Hybrid MAX is not simply the standard hybrid’s leather-seat package.

models.name: Sienna
models.role: Toyota people carrier with sliding rear doors
models.explanation: Sienna is Toyota’s minivan family. Sliding rear doors and a long passenger-focused cabin create a different use case from an SUV. A minivan is a body type, not a judgement about the driver.
models.tradeoff: Test child-seat access, third-row access and bags with all required seats in place. Sliding doors can be relevant in a tight parking space, but the overall van still needs to fit the garage.
models.compare: Compare Sienna with Highlander and Grand Highlander when passenger access matters. More SUV-like styling does not automatically provide a better people-carrying solution.
models.scenario: A family loads children several times a day in narrow parking spots. Include door access in the comparison rather than considering only seat count.
models.power: Recent Canadian Sienna generations use hybrid power. Older Siennas can have different engines, so ask for the year. AWD availability is a separate version detail.

models.name: Tacoma
models.explanation: Tacoma is Toyota’s midsize pickup family. Tundra is the larger pickup family; TRD is not the name of every Toyota truck. Cab, bed and mechanical configuration define the particular truck.
models.tradeoff: A pickup must meet the load job, not just look capable. Verify payload and towing for the exact configuration and keep the physical bed dimensions separate from the cabin size.
models.compare: Compare Tacoma with Tundra on actual load, bed and parking requirements. Do not assume the highest advertised capacity applies to the truck in a particular listing.
models.memory: Tacoma = midsize pickup; Tundra = larger pickup
models.scenario: A driver carries long equipment but parks in a small stall. Bed length and total vehicle length need checking together.
models.power: Current-generation engine/hybrid choices differ from older Tacomas. An i-FORCE MAX hybrid badge describes a powertrain; it is not the truck’s payload rating.

models.name: Tundra
models.explanation: Tundra is Toyota’s full-size pickup family. A full-size class offers a different starting role from Tacoma, but the exact cab, bed and engine still determine the configuration.
models.tradeoff: Larger trucks require a realistic parking and load assessment. Optional equipment and passengers can affect how much payload remains; the badge does not replace the vehicle’s actual labels.
models.compare: Compare Tundra with Tacoma and exact F-150/Silverado/Sierra/Ram configurations, matching the job and year rather than comparing only base prices.
models.scenario: Two Tundras have different bed and cab layouts. Treat them as different configurations before claiming the same load capacity.
models.power: Gas and hybrid versions have different mechanical specifications. A hybrid pickup is not automatically designed around the same efficiency priorities as a small hybrid commuter.

models.name: 4Runner & Land Cruiser
models.explanation: 4Runner and Land Cruiser are distinct Toyota SUV families with utility/off-road roles. They are separate from the brand’s everyday crossover names, even when shoppers compare them for family use.
models.tradeoff: Capability-oriented hardware may be useful for a specific job, but test daily access, comfort, size and luggage needs. Marketing about adventure does not specify the limits of every version.
models.compare: Compare these exact families with Highlander for a different road/utility balance. Verify seat configuration and tow limits; do not infer them from a rugged silhouette.
models.memory: 4Runner/Land Cruiser = utility families, not RAV4 trims
models.scenario: A friend never leaves paved roads but likes the look. Help them separate the styling preference from a need for particular off-road hardware.
models.power: Powertrains and architectures change across generations. A current hybrid specification should not be applied to an older V6/V8 example you see on the road.

models.name: bZ / bZ4X & Toyota electric names
models.explanation: Toyota’s bZ/bZ4X names identify battery-electric SUV products in relevant years. Naming changes are a reason to ask the year, not assume that every Toyota with a battery is the same sort of hybrid.
models.tradeoff: A battery-electric vehicle needs a charging plan. Compare the exact battery/range and charging specification, cabin and trips, rather than assuming Toyota’s conventional-hybrid routine applies.
models.compare: Compare a battery-electric Toyota with RAV4 Hybrid or Plug-in Hybrid by energy system first. bZ/bZ4X is not simply the electric trim name on a Corolla.
models.memory: bZ/bZ4X = battery-electric, not a conventional hybrid
models.scenario: A friend wants to put petrol in an all-electric Toyota as a backup. Explain why battery-electric and plug-in hybrid are different systems.
models.power: Battery-electric vehicles use motors and an externally charged battery, without a petrol engine for backup. Exact names and availability must be confirmed for the Canadian model year.

workshops.subtitle: Hybrid names, seating rows and pickup sizes.

pages.title: Corolla versus Corolla Cross
pages.text: Corolla names the lower-car family; Corolla Cross names a different SUV family. Similar names are a useful memory connection, but not proof of identical dimensions, seats or engines.
pages.example: A friend says they prefer the Cross for a higher seat. Understand that body preference before comparing the exact version’s price.
paragraphs: Cross identifies the separate SUV family, not a trim that turns every Corolla into an SUV.

pages.title: Hybrid versus Plug-in Hybrid
pages.text: Conventional hybrids combine an engine and electric assistance without a routine external plug. A plug-in hybrid adds an externally rechargeable battery. Older Prime naming is worth recognizing in used listings.
pages.example: A buyer has no reliable charger. Their comparison between a conventional hybrid and a plug-in should include the actual energy routine and price difference.
paragraphs: Plug-in refers to an externally rechargeable battery; it does not mean the vehicle has no petrol engine.

models.name: WRX

models.compare: Compare WRX with actual performance-sedan alternatives and with BRZ only after distinguishing sedan/AWD versus two-door/rear-drive roles.

models.name: BRZ

name: Ford
intro: Ford is an American brand with pickups, SUVs, commercial vans and the Mustang sports-car family. Learn the job before the badge: F-150, Ranger and Maverick are different pickup sizes; Bronco and Bronco Sport are different families; Mustang Mach-E is a separate electric SUV.
naming: XL, XLT, Lariat and other grades describe particular versions, not every Ford family. EcoBoost is turbo-engine branding used on different engines. Raptor identifies particular performance/utility versions. F-150 Lightning and Mustang Mach-E need separate electric-vehicle specifications.

models.power: F-150 configurations differ by cab, bed, engine, axle and equipment. A towing headline can be the maximum for one configuration, not the rating of a truck in a listing. F-150 Lightning is a separately specified electric truck.

models.power: Battery-electric. Battery/drive and capability depend on configuration. Do not treat maximum range and maximum towing advertisements as one guaranteed loaded-trip result.

name: Ram
intro: Ram is an American truck and commercial-vehicle brand. You may hear older pickups called Dodge Ram, but current Ram branding, truck class, cab/bed configuration and equipment grade are separate ideas. Begin with 1500 versus 2500/3500, then the specific work a truck must do.
naming: 1500, 2500 and 3500 are truck-class/model names, not universal payload values in kilograms. Big Horn, Laramie, Rebel and other grades describe versions. A Tradesman name on one product does not identify every Ram’s engine or body.

models.explanation: Ram 1500 is the brand’s light-duty full-size pickup family. Light-duty is a class description, not a statement that the truck has one fixed capacity.
models.tradeoff: Check cab/bed layout, actual payload and towing for the configuration. Passengers and accessories use load capacity; a premium trim does not create a universal tow rating.
models.compare: Compare Ram 1500 with matched F-150, Sierra 1500, Silverado 1500 and Tundra configurations for the actual job.
models.scenario: A friend assumes the number on the side tells them how much weight to load. Show why the vehicle’s actual labels and manual are needed.
models.power: Engines and hybrid-assistance systems have changed by year. A new or returning engine option does not describe every Ram 1500 on the street.

models.explanation: Ram 2500 is a heavier-duty pickup class than 1500. It exists for different load/use requirements, not simply as the 1500’s luxury equipment grade.
models.tradeoff: A more work-focused class can be unnecessary for ordinary use. Verify the actual load requirements, dimensions and running costs instead of buying the biggest class by default.
models.compare: Compare specific 2500 and 1500 configurations on the job and ratings. Diesel/gas choice and equipment also need matching.
models.scenario: A driver has no heavy-load requirement but likes the number. Explain what moving truck class is intended to change before discussing luxury options.
models.power: Gas and diesel engine choices depend on year/configuration. Diesel is a fuel/engine system, not a synonym for all heavy-duty trucks.

models.explanation: Ram 3500 is another heavy-duty pickup class, with configurations intended for different demanding load tasks. Single versus dual rear wheel is a configuration distinction, not a separate brand.
models.tradeoff: Use the exact vehicle’s load ratings and the actual loaded trailer requirements. More wheels or a larger model number alone cannot determine a safe loading plan.
models.compare: Compare matched heavy-duty configurations rather than a 3500 headline maximum with an unrelated 2500 base model.
models.scenario: A friend shows a dual-rear-wheel truck. You can recognize a configuration clue while still needing the model/year and load labels.
models.power: Engine, rear-wheel arrangement, axle and equipment affect capability. The family/class name is not enough to calculate payload or towing.

models.name: ProMaster
models.explanation: ProMaster is Ram’s commercial van family. A tall cargo van and a pickup solve different loading and access tasks, even if both can be used for work.
models.tradeoff: Check roof height, wheelbase, interior dimensions and the specific conversion. A camper or passenger conversion may change how the available load capacity is used.
models.compare: Compare ProMaster with exact Transit or other vans for the real cargo/interior task. A pickup’s open bed is not a substitute for an enclosed standing-height workspace.
models.memory: ProMaster = van, not a pickup trim
models.scenario: A friend wants a work van to carry tall equipment. Measure the inside and the doors, not only the vehicle’s outside height.
models.power: Powertrain and configuration are year/product-specific. Electric or other variants, where offered, require their own availability and charging checks.

name: Mitsubishi
intro: Mitsubishi is a Japanese brand whose familiar Canadian SUV names include Outlander, Outlander PHEV, RVR and Eclipse Cross. Learn the plug-in distinction carefully: similar body names do not make gas and plug-in versions the same energy system.
naming: Outlander is a family; PHEV means plug-in hybrid electric vehicle. ES, SE, SEL and GT are equipment grades whose contents vary by year. S-AWC is a drivetrain/control branding context, not a battery size or seat count. Eclipse Cross and new Eclipse electric naming need a complete model year and name.
warning: The course includes selected Canadian families plus explicitly labelled older/current road-recognition examples. Check the exact year, body, engine/drive configuration and current availability before using specifications or prices. Selected Canadian model families and clearly labelled recognition examples. Model year, exact version and availability must be checked before using a specification or price.

models.name: Outlander
models.explanation: Outlander is Mitsubishi’s family-SUV name, distinct from the separately specified Outlander PHEV product. A new generation can change mechanical details and seating arrangements.
models.tradeoff: Check actual seating and luggage with the required rows in use. An occasional back row, when fitted, does not guarantee that every adult will be comfortable on a long trip.
models.compare: Compare Outlander with Outlander PHEV on exact powertrain, price and charging needs; compare with RVR for a smaller role.
models.memory: Outlander = ask gas or PHEV and which year
models.scenario: A friend offers an Outlander for a group trip. Confirm the actual usable seats and remaining bags space before relying on the family name.
models.power: Gas and newer mild-hybrid-assistance specifications differ by generation. Do not infer external charging from the presence of any hybrid-related technology.

models.name: Outlander PHEV
models.role: Mitsubishi SUV with an externally rechargeable battery
models.explanation: Outlander PHEV is a plug-in-hybrid SUV product combining a combustion engine with electric propulsion and an externally rechargeable battery. It is not a battery-only EV.
models.tradeoff: It makes sense to evaluate a real charging routine along with longer-trip engine use. Seat/cargo fit and purchase price still need a separate comparison.
models.compare: Compare Outlander PHEV with a conventional hybrid and a battery-only SUV by how each uses energy. A plug-in badge does not guarantee zero petrol use on every trip.
models.memory: PHEV = plug-in battery plus an engine
models.scenario: A commuter can charge reliably overnight but sometimes takes long trips. Explain the two energy sources without promising a fixed electric range in all weather.
models.power: Plug-in-hybrid. External charging and engine/motor operation are different from a conventional hybrid routine. Exact battery/range and charging hardware are model-year-specific.

price.note: Manufacturer Canadian starting MSRP reference for the 2026 product, checked November 8, 2026. Extra charges, taxes, options and current availability require an itemized quote; incentives are not assumed.

models.name: RVR
models.explanation: RVR is Mitsubishi’s smaller crossover family in Canada. Related international ASX naming and generations should not be assumed mechanically identical to every Canadian RVR.
models.tradeoff: Check the exact year, rear-seat/cargo fit and drivetrain. A family’s presence in an overseas video is not evidence that the Canadian version has the same engine.
models.compare: Compare RVR with Outlander for size/seat needs, using actual dimensions rather than a brand-wide size assumption.
models.scenario: A friend found an ASX review abroad and applies all its specifications to a Canadian RVR. Ask whether the year and product actually match.
models.power: Gas engine and driven-wheel choices depend on Canadian model year and version. Market-specific naming needs a specification check.

models.name: Eclipse Cross / Eclipse recognition
models.role: Mitsubishi names that need the full body and year
models.explanation: Eclipse Cross is an SUV/crossover family, distinct from older Eclipse sports coupes. New Eclipse electric naming also makes the full name and year essential; the shared word does not define one unchanged car.
models.tradeoff: Identify the actual body and powertrain first. A historic sports-car image or engine specification should not be applied to a crossover or newly introduced EV.
models.compare: Compare Eclipse Cross with RVR and Outlander for the SUV role. Treat older Eclipse coupes and newer electric names as separate recognition/product contexts.
models.memory: Cross changes the family; year resolves the name
models.scenario: A friend says they saw an Eclipse. Ask whether they mean an older coupe, an Eclipse Cross SUV or a new product, before picturing it.
models.power: Gas, historical sports-car and new electric products need separate mechanical specifications. A reused name is not a promise of unchanged propulsion.

name: Jeep
intro: Jeep is an American brand, not a generic word for every SUV. Learn Wrangler, Grand Cherokee and Compass first, then separate Gladiator pickups and the Wagoneer names. Utility badges, body families and electrified systems describe different things.
naming: 4xe identifies plug-in-hybrid products in relevant years, not every Jeep with four-wheel drive. Grand Cherokee L identifies a different three-row body role. Rubicon, Trailhawk and other names describe particular versions; their meaning depends on the model and year.
warning: The course includes selected Canadian families plus explicitly labelled older/current road-recognition examples. Check the exact year, body, engine/drive configuration and current availability before using specifications or prices. The families below are selected for learning and recognition. Check the linked official range for current Canadian availability, model years, equipment and pricing. A familiar name may remain on used cars after new-car availability changes.

models.name: Wrangler
models.explanation: Wrangler is a distinctive upright SUV family with an off-road role. Different bodies and versions have different seating, doors, equipment and powertrains.
models.tradeoff: The Wrangler belongs in a comparison for jeep’s upright off-road family. Check actual passenger fit, cargo access, exterior dimensions and the exact version’s running costs. Its category is a starting point, not a promise that it fits every person or task.
models.compare: Compare real daily comfort, access and use before deciding that an off-road-focused vehicle is the best commuter. A 4xe badge calls for understanding plug-in charging.
models.scenario: A friend mentions a Wrangler. Explain its role as jeep’s upright off-road family, then ask for the year, powertrain and equipment before comparing it with another Jeep.
models.power: Wrangler gas and 4xe plug-in-hybrid versions are different powertrains in relevant years. Door/body choices and equipment also vary. A 4xe badge is not simply another word for ordinary four-wheel drive.

models.name: Gladiator

models.explanation: Gladiator is Jeep’s pickup family, visually related to the Wrangler world but with an open cargo bed and its own configuration. It is not merely a Wrangler with the rear seats folded.
