models.power: Engine/drivetrain and tow equipment depend on year/version. Utility trim names do not replace the configured vehicle’s ratings.

models.name: Wagoneer & Grand Wagoneer
models.explanation: Wagoneer and Grand Wagoneer are large SUV family names in the Jeep-associated range. Grand Wagoneer positioning and naming can change, so use the exact product/year rather than assuming it is a trim on every Grand Cherokee.
models.tradeoff: Compare seating, cargo with all rows up, total exterior size and the equipment you value. More luxury equipment is not proof of more usable seats.
models.compare: Compare these exact large SUV products with Grand Cherokee L and large competitors such as Tahoe/Suburban or Expedition.
models.memory: Wagoneer is not simply Grand Cherokee with a package
models.scenario: A friend uses Grand Cherokee and Grand Wagoneer interchangeably. Clarify the family before discussing dimensions or price.
models.power: Engine and drivetrain choices are year-specific. Check current naming and Canadian ordering availability before using an older brochure as a new-car specification.

models.name: Cherokee & Renegade — road recognition
models.role: Jeep names to recognize across model years
models.explanation: Cherokee and Renegade names appear on different Jeep SUV families across years. They remain useful for road and used-car recognition even while new-car lineups change.
models.tradeoff: Ask the year, condition and actual configuration. A familiar name returning in a newer product does not freeze the previous generation’s dimensions or engine.
models.compare: Compare each specific generation with Compass or Grand Cherokee by role. Do not drop the word Grand and assume it is the same family.
models.memory: Cherokee and Grand Cherokee are not interchangeable names
models.scenario: A friend shares a used Cherokee listing. Identify its own family and year instead of reading a current Grand Cherokee specification.
models.power: Powertrain availability is generation-specific. This recognition lesson does not claim all these names are currently orderable in Canada.

name: Mazda
intro: Mazda is a Japanese brand. Its range includes low everyday cars, several sizes of SUV and the small MX-5 sports car. Begin with the shape and number of seating rows; the similar-looking CX names become easier when each has a job.
naming: Mazda3 is the compact car family; Sport means its hatchback body in Canada. CX names identify SUV families. GX, GS and GT are equipment grades on various Canadian models, not different manufacturers. Turbo describes an engine feature. RF is an MX-5 roof version.
warning: The course includes selected Canadian families plus explicitly labelled older/current road-recognition examples. Check the exact year, body, engine/drive configuration and current availability before using specifications or prices. CX-30, CX-5 and CX-50 are not a simple small/medium/large numerical ladder. CX-70 has two seating rows; CX-90 has three. Mazda Canada currently labels CX-50 models as sold out/previous models; learn them for road and used-car recognition.

models.name: Mazda3 Sedan
models.role: Low everyday car with a separate trunk
models.explanation: The Mazda3 Sedan is Mazda’s compact passenger car with a separate trunk lid. It sits lower than Mazda’s SUVs. “Mazda3” is the family; GX, GS or GT describes equipment on a particular Canadian version.
models.tradeoff: Consider it when you want an everyday car without an SUV shape. Check the rear-seat fit and trunk opening with your own passengers and luggage. A separate trunk can conceal bags, but a large box may be harder to load through its opening.
models.compare: Compare Mazda3 Sedan with Mazda3 Sport for the cargo opening, and with CX-30 for a taller body and seating position. Do not assume that an SUV badge guarantees more usable room.
models.scenario: A commuter carries a backpack and groceries, and parks in a tight stall. Start by comparing the sedan with the hatchback, then test the trunk with the largest thing they regularly carry.
models.power: The Canadian Mazda3 range offers different engine/drivetrain versions, including available turbo power and all-wheel drive. Those are version choices, not features of every Mazda3.

price.label: Mazda3 GX Sedan FWD
price.note: Starting Canadian MSRP; excludes freight/preparation, taxes and other applicable charges. Actual sale price and availability vary.

models.name: Mazda3 Sport
models.role: Low everyday car with a lifting hatch
models.explanation: In Canada, Mazda3 Sport names the hatchback body of the Mazda3 family. Its rear door lifts with the rear window. The word Sport here does not mean every version is a dedicated racing or high-performance car.
models.tradeoff: The hatch opening can make some bulky objects easier to load. Look at both the shape of the opening and the space with the rear seats in use. A hatchback’s external outline does not tell you how comfortably three adults will fit in its back seat.
models.compare: Choose between Mazda3 Sedan and Sport by testing access and everyday practicality. Compare Sport with CX-30 if you want a higher seating position, rather than assuming they are the same car at different heights.
models.memory: Sport = hatch, not automatically a faster engine
models.scenario: Your friend says “I got the Sport.” Ask if they mean the hatchback body, then ask which engine and trim.
models.power: The Sport can have different Canadian engine and drivetrain configurations. Check the specific year and grade; the body-style word does not settle its power output.

models.name: CX-30
models.explanation: CX-30 is Mazda’s smaller SUV family. It gives you an SUV-shaped alternative to the low Mazda3. It is a different family from CX-3, an older small Mazda SUV you may still hear about.
models.tradeoff: Its smaller SUV footprint may be relevant in tight parking, but verify dimensions and visibility rather than relying on the word subcompact. Test access, rear-seat fit and the cargo space you need; a higher roof is not a promise of generous room everywhere.
models.compare: CX-30 versus Mazda3 is partly a body and seating-position choice. CX-30 versus CX-5 is a comparison of two different SUV families. The 30 in CX-30 does not make it larger than every model with a one-digit number.
models.memory: CX-30 = the smaller current Mazda SUV
models.scenario: A friend likes the idea of an SUV but rarely carries passengers. Compare their parking and entry/exit needs with the Mazda3 before paying for a different body style.
models.power: Canadian CX-30 models have standard AWD and available turbo power. Turbo versions are not identical in output or price to the non-turbo versions.

price.label: CX-30 GX AWD
price.note: Starting Canadian MSRP; excludes freight/preparation, taxes and other applicable charges. Actual sale price and availability vary.

models.name: CX-5
models.explanation: CX-5 is a five-seat compact SUV with two seating rows. It is an important name to recognize separately from CX-30 and CX-50. A family name can continue across a redesign, so a picture of an older CX-5 does not show every detail of the newest one.
models.tradeoff: It belongs on a shortlist for people who need everyday passenger and cargo versatility without a third row. Confirm the exact dimensions, rear-seat access and visibility of the generation you are considering.
models.compare: Compare it with CX-30 for size and packaging, with CX-50 for a different compact-SUV design, and with CX-90 if an extra seating row is a real requirement. A higher trim cannot add a missing seating row to the CX-5.
models.scenario: A household with two adults and two children wants an SUV. Their question is whether a two-row CX-5 fits their seats and stroller, not whether the largest model number sounds more impressive.
models.power: The 2027 Canadian CX-5 launch specifies a 2.5-litre four-cylinder engine, automatic transmission and AWD. Check year-specific specifications instead of carrying older turbo-version assumptions into the new generation.

price.label: CX-5 GX AWD
price.note: Starting Canadian MSRP; excludes freight/preparation, taxes and other applicable charges. Actual sale price and availability vary.

models.name: CX-50 & CX-50 Hybrid
models.role: Another compact SUV to recognize on the road
models.explanation: CX-50 is another Mazda compact SUV, distinct from CX-5. The Canadian previous-model range also includes a CX-50 Hybrid. Mazda Canada marks these models sold out on the range page checked for this course; that is not a statement that you will never see one used or on the road.
models.tradeoff: Recognize the broad compact-SUV role, then inspect the exact vehicle. Outdoor styling does not by itself establish towing, off-road ability or ground clearance; those require the actual specification and limits.
models.compare: CX-50 and CX-5 overlap in broad role. Compare the specific year’s cabin, dimensions, powertrain and availability. Do not assume that 50 means ten times a CX-5 or automatically means a three-row vehicle.
models.memory: CX-50 = a different compact SUV, not a three-row CX-5
models.scenario: A friend mentions a used CX-50 Hybrid. You can place it as a compact SUV, then ask about the year, condition and hybrid version before discussing value.
models.power: The gas and Hybrid versions are different powertrain choices. A conventional hybrid is not a plug-in hybrid; do not expect an external charging routine merely because the name includes Hybrid.

models.name: CX-70
models.explanation: CX-70 is a larger Mazda SUV with two seating rows and five seats. Its main distinction from the related CX-90 is the two-row arrangement. Fewer rows do not automatically mean a tiny exterior.
models.tradeoff: It may make sense when a buyer wants a larger SUV but does not need a third row. Check the cargo area with the seats in use and the physical size against the parking space. Extra vehicle length can be a compromise even without extra seats.
models.compare: CX-70 versus CX-90 starts with two rows versus three. CX-70 versus CX-5 also needs a size and powertrain comparison; a missing third row does not put all two-row SUVs in the same size class.
models.memory: 70 = two rows in Mazda’s larger SUV pair
models.scenario: Two people carry equipment rather than extra passengers. Their starting question is how the CX-70 cargo layout fits that equipment, not how many occasional seats they can claim.
models.power: Mazda offers CX-70 mild-hybrid inline-six and plug-in-hybrid versions. Inline-six describes six cylinders in a row. Mild hybrid and plug-in hybrid have different battery/charging arrangements; a mild hybrid is not a substitute for a plug-in electric driving plan.

models.name: CX-90
models.role: Larger SUV with a third seating row
models.explanation: CX-90 is Mazda’s three-row SUV family. Seating capacity varies with the configuration, so check the actual seat layout rather than treating every CX-90 as identical. Three rows create a different passenger-carrying role from CX-70.
models.tradeoff: A third row is useful only if it works for your passengers. Sit in it, check access and see how much luggage space remains with all required seats upright. Larger exterior dimensions can make parking and manoeuvring less convenient.
models.compare: CX-90 versus CX-70 is a seating-layout decision before it is a prestige decision. If the third row is unnecessary, compare the two-row alternatives and total running costs rather than assuming the largest SUV is the best answer.
models.memory: 90 = three rows in Mazda’s larger SUV pair
models.scenario: A driver regularly carries more than five people. CX-90 belongs on the seating checklist; CX-70 does not solve that requirement merely by having a high equipment grade.
models.power: The range includes mild-hybrid inline-six and plug-in-hybrid configurations. The PHEV combines a petrol engine and externally rechargeable battery; do not confuse it with a fully electric SUV.

price.label: CX-90 MHEV GS
price.note: Announced for arrival in winter; starting CAD MSRP, excluding freight/PDE, taxes and other applicable charges. Confirm arrival and availability.

models.name: MX-5 & MX-5 RF
models.role: Small sports car for two people
models.explanation: MX-5 is Mazda’s two-seat roadster. A roadster is a small open-top sports car. Soft Top and RF describe roof versions; RF uses a retracting roof design. Neither turns it into a family hatchback.
models.tradeoff: The appeal is a small sports-car experience, with obvious compromises in passengers and luggage. Test seat comfort and entry/exit. A two-seat car is a poor answer if you regularly need to carry a third person, regardless of how much you like its design.
models.compare: MX-5 is not the next step up from a Mazda3 in a size ladder. It is a different job. Compare Soft Top and RF for roof operation and your preferences, then compare the exact transmissions and equipment.
models.scenario: Someone wants a second car for enjoyable trips with one passenger. Another person needs to take two children to school. The same MX-5 cannot meet both passenger requirements.
models.power: The 2026 Canadian MX-5 uses a 2.0-litre four-cylinder petrol engine. Transmission availability depends on the version. A manual asks the driver to select gears and operate the clutch; an automatic changes gears without that routine.

price.label: MX-5 GS Soft Top
price.note: Starting Canadian MSRP; excludes freight/preparation, taxes and other applicable charges. Actual sale price and availability vary.

name: BMW
intro: BMW is a German brand with numbered passenger-car families, X SUV families, performance variants and electric cars. The range is easier to understand when you separate the main family from the long string of letters and numbers that follows.
naming: A 3 Series is a family. 330i, M340i and their year-dependent replacements identify versions. X usually identifies an SUV family. xDrive means BMW all-wheel drive. M Sport is an equipment/styling line; an M3 is a dedicated performance model. BMW’s i electric names and engine suffixes need context, not a one-letter rule.
warning: The course includes selected Canadian families plus explicitly labelled older/current road-recognition examples. Check the exact year, body, engine/drive configuration and current availability before using specifications or prices. Do not read a badge such as 330 as a literal 3.30-litre engine specification. Names change between years: the new electric i3 sedan is not the old compact i3 city car. Availability also differs between Canada and Europe.

models.name: 2 Series
models.explanation: 2 Series includes names used for different body and mechanical layouts. A 2 Series Coupe is a two-door car. The 2 Series Gran Coupe is a separate four-door family; Gran Coupe is a naming convention, not proof of two doors.
models.tradeoff: If access to the rear seats matters, compare the actual bodies. A smaller-looking car can be easier to place in a parking spot but less convenient for regularly loading passengers. Do not transfer a Coupe review’s handling conclusions to a Gran Coupe just because both say 2.
models.compare: Compare 2 Series Coupe with 4 Series Coupe for the two-door role. Compare 2 Series Gran Coupe with 3 Series Sedan for four-door practicality, using the exact versions.
models.memory: 2 = start small, then check Coupe or Gran Coupe
models.scenario: A friend says “a 2 Series.” Your useful follow-up is “the two-door Coupe or the four-door Gran Coupe?” before discussing the engine.
models.power: The mechanical layout and powertrain depend on which 2 Series family and year you mean. M235, M240 and M2 are not interchangeable badges for the same car.

models.name: 3 Series
models.explanation: The 3 Series is BMW’s familiar everyday sports-sedan family. “Sports sedan” describes its market role, not a measured promise that every driver will prefer it. The family name does not tell you which engine or equipment is installed.
models.tradeoff: It belongs in a comparison when you want four doors and a lower car rather than an SUV. Try the rear seat and trunk with your own needs. More engine power may change acceleration without improving either of those spaces.
models.compare: Compare 3 Series with 5 Series for a larger sedan, with X3 for an SUV alternative, and with 4 Series for related coupe/Gran Coupe roles. The M3 is a performance model; a regular 3 Series with an M Sport package is not mechanically equivalent.
models.scenario: A friend says they chose a 3 instead of an X3 because they prefer a lower car. You can understand the body-style trade-off before needing to know their exact engine.
models.power: A 330i badge does not literally state a 3.3-litre displacement. Versions and naming are changing; read the Canadian year-specific engine and drivetrain details.

price.label: 330i xDrive Sedan — retailer MSRP reference
price.note: Historical Canadian retailer MSRP reference; the source’s promotion has expired. Excludes freight/fees, licensing and tax. Confirm the current year, configuration and itemized quote.

models.name: 4 Series
models.explanation: The 4 Series name covers coupe, convertible and Gran Coupe forms. Coupe is the two-door closed-roof role; convertible has an opening roof; Gran Coupe is a four-door shape with a more coupe-like outline. Confirm the exact body before comparing.
models.tradeoff: A sloping roof and different door arrangement can affect access and usable room. Test the space rather than deciding from a stylish side profile. A convertible also asks you to consider the roof’s operation and cargo arrangement.
models.compare: Compare a 4 Series Coupe with a 2 Series Coupe for two-door choices. Compare a 4 Series Gran Coupe with a 3 Series Sedan if rear access matters. The electric i4 belongs in the conversation but needs a charging plan.
models.memory: 4 = ask which roof and how many doors
models.scenario: A friend says “four-door coupe.” They may mean a 4 Series Gran Coupe, not that somebody miscounted the doors.
models.power: Gas 4 Series and all-electric i4 names can look related but describe different powertrains. Dedicated M4 performance versions are not the same as an M Sport styling/equipment package.

models.name: 5 Series & i5
models.explanation: 5 Series is a larger sedan family than the 3 Series. “Executive” is a market category, not a requirement that the owner have a particular job. The i5 is the electric sedan in this part of BMW’s range.
models.tradeoff: A larger cabin may be relevant to comfort, but physical fit and ride preference need checking in the actual vehicle. Extra size can also make a garage or tight city parking more awkward. Larger is not a free improvement in every situation.
models.compare: Compare 5 Series with 3 Series for size/role, and with 7 Series for the larger luxury-sedan role. Compare gas and i5 versions using charging access, efficiency, range needs and price, not just power output.
models.scenario: A driver often carries an adult in the rear seat. They should test that passenger’s fit and comfort in both the 3 and 5 rather than buying the larger number automatically.
models.power: A 5 Series badge and an i5 badge do not imply the same fuel source. BMW also has performance versions; identify the exact model year and variant before comparing engines.

models.name: 7 Series & i7
models.explanation: 7 Series is BMW’s large luxury-sedan family; i7 identifies its all-electric relative. Flagship means a brand’s prominent upper-end product. It does not mean that its size or cost makes it the best car for every owner.
models.tradeoff: A buyer may prioritize rear-seat comfort and extensive equipment. They must also consider the vehicle’s physical size, purchase cost and the expense of maintaining its particular equipment. Luxury features can be useful preferences rather than must-haves.
models.compare: Compare 7 Series with 5 Series for the size and luxury role. Compare i7 with combustion/hybrid variants on actual use and charging. Do not confuse 7 Series, a sedan family, with X7, an SUV family.
models.scenario: Your friend discusses being driven rather than doing most of the driving. Rear-seat access, comfort and controls become relevant comparison criteria.
models.power: The 7 Series/i7 range includes different powertrains depending on year and market. A large luxury car does not always have a large number of cylinders; the i7 has electric motors instead.

models.name: X1 & X2
models.explanation: X1 is a smaller BMW SUV family. X2 occupies a related coupe-style SUV role with a different shape. “Coupe-style SUV” usually describes the roofline; it does not promise two doors.
models.tradeoff: Compare visibility, rear headroom and cargo access. A roof that looks sportier may matter less to someone who regularly carries tall rear-seat passengers. Measure the actual models rather than inferring space from their similar badges.
models.compare: X1 versus X3 is a smaller/larger SUV comparison. X1 versus X2 also asks how much you value the shape and practical packaging. Do not assume a European electric iX1 is sold in Canada because you found an overseas review.
models.memory: X1 = smaller SUV; X2 = check the roofline
models.scenario: A city driver likes a higher seating position but has a small parking stall. X1 belongs in the comparison, with its actual dimensions checked.
models.power: Canadian X1 engine/drivetrain availability is market-specific. xDrive means all-wheel drive, not that winter tires become unnecessary. AWD does not remove the need for appropriate tires and safe speeds.

price.label: X1 xDrive28i — retailer MSRP reference
price.note: Canadian retailer reference; historical offer context, not an active promotion. Base MSRP excludes the retailer’s listed freight/fees and tax. Confirm a current itemized quote.

models.name: X3
models.explanation: X3 is a BMW SUV family larger in role than X1. The X distinguishes it from the low 3 Series sedan. Similar numbers do not mean identical bodies or identical equipment.
models.tradeoff: Check its fit for passengers, loading and your parking space. A higher seating position is a preference some people value; it is not by itself evidence that a car is safer or more capable in every condition.
models.compare: X3 versus 3 Series is partly an SUV-versus-sedan choice. X3 versus X5 is a different-size SUV comparison. Use exact year specifications because redesigned generations can change size and engines.
models.scenario: A friend says “the X3 feels more useful for loading my gear.” Ask what the gear is and whether the actual hatch and seats solve that problem.
models.power: BMW’s engines and badge conventions change by generation. M Performance, M Sport equipment and dedicated M models are separate concepts; a letter on a trim list is not a complete mechanical description.

price.label: X3 30 xDrive — retailer MSRP reference
price.note: Historical Canadian retailer MSRP reference; the source’s promotion has expired. Excludes freight/fees, licensing and tax. Confirm the current year, configuration and itemized quote.

models.name: X5 & X6
models.explanation: X5 is a larger BMW SUV family. X6 uses the coupe-style SUV idea in a larger size class. These names describe families, not one engine. An xDrive50e version, for example, needs to be understood separately from a conventional gas version.
models.tradeoff: More vehicle can offer useful packaging but also demands more parking space and a realistic running-cost comparison. Check seat configuration, cargo measurements and tire costs for the actual version.
models.compare: Compare X5 with X3 when moving up in SUV size, and with X7 if extra seating is the central need. Compare X5 and X6 by their actual roof, rear-seat and load-space differences.
models.memory: X5 = larger SUV; X6 = different roof in that broad role
models.scenario: A household wants to replace an X3. Make them name the space problem first; a more powerful X3 would not necessarily fix it.
models.power: Plug-in-hybrid and other versions can have different charging needs, performance and weight. The suffix e on particular BMW model names can indicate a plug-in hybrid; verify the exact model rather than treating one letter as a universal law.

price.label: X5 xDrive40i — retailer MSRP reference
price.note: Historical Canadian retailer MSRP reference; the source’s promotion has expired. Excludes freight/fees, licensing and tax. Confirm the current year, configuration and itemized quote.

models.name: X7
models.role: Largest conventional BMW SUV family in this course
models.explanation: X7 is BMW’s large three-row SUV family. It fills a passenger-carrying role distinct from the 7 Series sedan. Three rows and the exact seat configuration matter more to a family than a vague “top model” label.
models.tradeoff: Check third-row access, adult fit and cargo with the seats upright. A larger SUV can help with seating needs while being harder to park; do not count the third row as useful until your passengers try it.
models.compare: Compare X7 with X5 if the third row is an actual requirement, and with 7 Series only after recognizing that sedan comfort and SUV versatility are different priorities.
models.scenario: A group regularly travels with more than five people. Start with seating configurations and luggage, then narrow the powertrain and trim.
models.power: Exact engines and seating configurations depend on model year and version. M-related equipment or engine choices do not substitute for checking the seating layout.

models.name: i4, i5, i7 & iX
models.role: BMW electric families and their different shapes
models.explanation: BMW’s electric names still describe different jobs: i4 is a lower four-door car, i5 and i7 occupy larger sedan roles, and iX is an electric SUV. The letter i is not enough to identify the body or size.
models.tradeoff: An electric car needs a charging routine that works where you live and travel. Check the specific version’s usable range information, charging capabilities, winter-trip needs and access to reliable charging. More advertised range is not the only ownership consideration.
models.compare: Compare i4 with other lower four-door choices, i5 with larger sedans, i7 with large luxury sedans and iX with SUVs. A newer i3 sedan is a separate product from the earlier small i3; always ask the year.
models.memory: Electric tells you the energy source, not the body style
models.scenario: A friend says “all BMW i cars are the same sort of car.” Explain the sedan/SUV distinction and ask which i-model they mean.
models.power: These named i families use electric propulsion. The final powertrain and drive configuration varies by version. Look up Canadian range/charging specifications rather than importing European test numbers.

name: Mercedes-Benz
intro: Mercedes-Benz is a German brand with passenger-car, SUV, electric, sports-car and luxury sub-brand names. Start with the central letter family, then learn what the extra numbers and words describe. A long badge becomes readable when it is split into pieces.
naming: C-, E- and S-Class identify different sedan families. GLA, GLC, GLE and GLS are SUV families. 4MATIC is Mercedes all-wheel drive. AMG identifies performance-related models/lines, but an AMG Line appearance package is not a dedicated Mercedes-AMG car. Maybach is a luxury sub-brand, not an engine size.
warning: The course includes selected Canadian families plus explicitly labelled older/current road-recognition examples. Check the exact year, body, engine/drive configuration and current availability before using specifications or prices. C 300 does not automatically mean a 3.0-litre engine. GLC Coupe can have four side doors. New electric CLA and GLC names coexist with familiar combustion names; model year and powertrain are essential. Historical GLB or older EQ names still matter for recognition even when current availability changes.

models.name: CLA
models.explanation: CLA is a smaller four-door Mercedes family. Mercedes has used coupe language for its lower, sloping-roof four-door body. The current Canadian range distinguishes an electric CLA sedan from familiar gas CLA Coupe versions, so the name needs a year and powertrain.
models.tradeoff: Compare rear headroom, access and charging needs instead of treating the badge as one timeless specification. A sporty outline can be attractive while still requiring a practical seating test.
models.compare: CLA versus C-Class compares different four-door families. A CLA electric sedan and a gas CLA are not the same energy choice, even if a friend shortens both names to CLA.
models.memory: CLA = compact four-door; ask electric or gas
models.scenario: A friend says they ordered the new CLA. Ask which model year and whether it is electric before discussing fuel or charging.
models.power: Electric and combustion versions have different systems. Do not use a gas CLA review to predict the battery, range or charging speed of the new electric sedan.

models.name: C-Class
models.explanation: C-Class is Mercedes’ core everyday sedan family. In the Canadian C 300 4MATIC example, C identifies the family, 300 is a version badge and 4MATIC identifies all-wheel drive. The badge is not a literal count of cylinders.
models.tradeoff: Consider it for a lower four-door car. Check the rear seat, trunk opening and your preferred controls in the exact year. Appearance packages may change the look without changing it into a dedicated AMG performance model.
models.compare: C-Class versus E-Class is a different-size sedan comparison. C-Class versus GLC is a sedan-versus-SUV comparison. A more expensive C-Class version does not automatically have more passenger room than an E-Class.
models.scenario: Your friend says “C 300 4MATIC.” You can translate it into the family, version and driven-wheel system before looking up the engine.
models.power: The 2026 Canadian C 300 4MATIC uses a turbo four-cylinder with mild-hybrid assistance. Mild-hybrid assistance does not make it a plug-in car you recharge for an electric commute.

price.label: C 300 4MATIC Sedan — retailer MSRP reference
price.note: Canadian retailer’s listed MSRP reference; excludes options, freight/fees and applicable taxes unless explicitly included by that retailer. Verify the exact configuration and current quote.

models.name: E-Class & E All-Terrain
models.explanation: E-Class occupies a larger sedan role than C-Class. E All-Terrain is a wagon-based member of the wider E family: an extended roof and rear hatch create a different cargo arrangement from a sedan trunk.
models.tradeoff: A larger car can be relevant to passenger comfort, while a wagon can help with particular loading tasks. Neither label guarantees the best fit for every adult or bulky item; measure and try the actual car.
models.compare: Compare C-Class and E-Class for different sedan roles. Compare E All-Terrain with an SUV such as GLE for the body/roof/loading choice; do not call every tall-looking wagon an SUV.
models.memory: E = larger sedan; All-Terrain = check the wagon body
models.scenario: Someone wants a lower car but carries bulky luggage. The wagon conversation is about the loading shape, not just a higher engine number.
models.power: E-family powertrains vary by year and version. E 350, E 450 and AMG E 53 HYBRID are different specifications; the larger version number is not a literal displacement formula.

models.name: S-Class & Mercedes-Maybach S-Class
models.explanation: S-Class is Mercedes’ large luxury-sedan family. Mercedes-Maybach S-Class adds a distinct luxury-focused range above ordinary S-Class positioning. Maybach is a sub-brand name, not a fuel type.
models.tradeoff: Think about who uses the rear seat, the value of the equipment to them, and the size of the car in everyday use. Expensive luxury equipment is not automatically helpful for a commuter with a tight garage and a limited budget.
models.compare: S-Class versus E-Class compares different luxury-sedan roles. S-Class versus GLS compares a sedan with a large SUV. Do not assume that S-Class and GLS have interchangeable seating or cargo arrangements.
models.memory: S = flagship sedan; Maybach = luxury sub-brand
models.scenario: A friend says “it is a Maybach.” Ask whether they mean an S-Class sedan or a GLS/EQS SUV before picturing the car.
models.power: Powertrain depends on the exact S-Class or Maybach version. The family and luxury sub-brand names do not tell you the number of cylinders or the fuel requirement.

models.name: GLA
models.explanation: GLA is a smaller Mercedes SUV family. It is useful to put it on the small-SUV shelf before memorizing the numbers after its name. A GLA is not a C-Class simply because both are Mercedes vehicles.
models.tradeoff: Check rear-seat and cargo fit carefully. Choosing the smaller SUV role may suit parking needs, but verify actual dimensions and sight lines. Body category alone cannot prove it is easier for every driver to manoeuvre.
models.compare: GLA versus GLC compares different SUV sizes/roles. GLA versus CLA also introduces a different body shape and seating position. Use the exact generations rather than assuming all names stay dimensionally fixed.
models.scenario: A friend wants the least bulky SUV on their shortlist. Begin with dimensions and visibility, not the claim that any SUV will be easy to park.
models.power: GLA 250 4MATIC and Mercedes-AMG GLA 35 are distinct versions. 4MATIC relates to driven wheels; AMG relates to performance positioning. They do not mean the same thing.

models.name: GLB — road & used-car recognition
models.role: Boxier Mercedes compact SUV to recognize
models.explanation: GLB is a Mercedes SUV family with a boxier outline than the GLA. It is included for road and used-car recognition. Its presence in an older review does not confirm that a new Canadian example is currently orderable.
models.tradeoff: Check the exact seating configuration, access and cargo arrangement. An occasional small third row, when fitted, is not the same thing as adult comfort for a long journey. Do not assume every GLB has the same seat count.
models.compare: Compare GLB with GLA for shape/packaging and with GLC for a different family role. Ask the year and confirm current availability before treating an old price or configuration as a new-car offer.
models.memory: GLB = boxier small SUV; verify year and seats
models.scenario: A friend offers a used GLB for a group trip. Before agreeing, confirm how many usable seats it actually has and how much luggage space remains.
models.power: Powertrain and seat configuration depend on the year and version. This recognition lesson is not a statement of current new-car availability.

models.name: GLC & GLC Coupe
models.explanation: GLC is a core Mercedes SUV family. GLC Coupe uses a coupe-style roof in the SUV category and can still have four side doors. The latest range also introduces a GLC Electric, so a complete name must include the powertrain.
models.tradeoff: Compare rear headroom, luggage access and visibility between SUV and Coupe bodies. A roofline preference is valid, but identify what practical compromises you are willing to accept.
models.compare: GLC versus C-Class compares an SUV with a sedan; GLC versus GLE compares different SUV families. A GLC 350e plug-in hybrid is not simply a more powerful version of an identical gas-only system.
models.memory: GLC = core SUV, even when the roof says Coupe
models.scenario: Your friend says their GLC Coupe has four doors. That fits the manufacturer’s naming: coupe-style refers to the shape here.
models.power: Gas, plug-in-hybrid and newly introduced electric GLC names require exact year/version checks. A plug-in hybrid combines a combustion engine with an externally rechargeable battery.

models.name: GLE & GLE Coupe
models.explanation: GLE occupies a larger SUV role than GLC. GLE Coupe is a differently shaped member of the broad range. The numbers and extra words identify different engines, performance systems and versions.
models.tradeoff: Check the exact passenger configuration, cargo space and exterior dimensions. A bigger vehicle can help a genuine space need while creating parking and cost compromises. Do not decide a seating requirement from the family name alone.
models.compare: GLE versus GLC is a different-size SUV comparison. GLE versus GLS asks whether the larger three-row role is needed. GLE Coupe versus SUV also calls for a rear-headroom and loading comparison.
models.memory: GLE = larger SUV, below GLS in this course’s role map
models.scenario: A friend says the GLE is better than the GLC. Ask what they need more of: a particular kind of room, comfort, towing specification or performance.
models.power: GLE gas, plug-in-hybrid and AMG versions can have different mechanical systems. Confirm the exact Canadian year; AMG HYBRID and a regular plug-in version are not interchangeable names.

models.name: GLS & Mercedes-Maybach GLS
models.explanation: GLS is Mercedes’ large three-row SUV family. Mercedes-Maybach GLS is a luxury-focused version family, with its own seating/equipment priorities. More luxury does not necessarily mean more passenger capacity.
models.tradeoff: Test the third row and luggage space for your actual group. A luxury-oriented seat layout may be less suitable for carrying many people than a different configuration, despite a higher price.
models.compare: GLS versus GLE begins with real seating/cargo requirements. GLS versus S-Class is a different-body comparison. Ordinary GLS and Maybach GLS should be checked separately for the exact seat arrangement.
models.memory: GLS = large three-row SUV; Maybach changes the brief
models.scenario: A friend assumes the most expensive GLS is always the best people carrier. Look at the actual seat configuration before accepting that claim.
models.power: GLS 450, GLS 580, AMG GLS 63 and Maybach GLS 600 are distinct versions. The number is not a universal cylinder-count or displacement code.

models.name: G-Class
models.explanation: G-Class is the distinctive upright, boxy Mercedes SUV family, often called a G-Wagon. It is a different family from GLA, GLC, GLE and GLS. Those shared letters do not turn it into the last step of a simple family-SUV size ladder.
models.tradeoff: Its distinctive look and off-road role may matter to some owners. They still need to consider everyday access, comfort, physical size and costs. An off-road reputation does not remove the need to read the exact limits or drive appropriately.
models.compare: Compare it with other SUVs on the actual task rather than the attention its shape attracts. The electric G and gas versions also need separate energy and charging discussions.
models.memory: G = the very boxy one, not shorthand for every GL model
models.scenario: A friend points to an upright SUV with a rear-mounted spare wheel. Treat that as a clue, then check the badge and other details rather than claiming an exact engine from the silhouette.
models.power: The current range includes gas G 550, Mercedes-AMG G 63 and an electric G 580. A familiar body shape does not mean every version burns petrol.

models.name: EQE, EQS & new electric names
models.role: Mercedes electric families and naming changes
models.explanation: EQE and EQS have been used for electric sedan and SUV families. Sedan and SUV must be stated because the same broad name does not settle the body. New CLA and GLC Electric naming shows why learning only the prefix EQ is no longer enough.
models.tradeoff: Check charging access, actual trip length, winter requirements and the specific model’s Canadian range information. Electric does not mean small, inexpensive or identical in charging performance.
models.compare: EQE Sedan versus EQE SUV is a body comparison. EQS versus EQE also compares different family roles. A new CLA Electric is not identified by an EQ prefix, so read the full model description.
models.memory: Energy source and body are two separate labels
models.scenario: Your friend says they bought an EQE. Ask “sedan or SUV?” before forming a picture of it, then ask which year and version.
models.power: These electric families use electric motors instead of a petrol engine. Battery/range and charging specifications vary; do not transfer numbers between the sedan and SUV.

models.name: CLE, SL & AMG GT
models.explanation: CLE names coupe and cabriolet families; cabriolet means convertible. SL is a roadster family. AMG GT includes distinct sports-car forms, so the full name and body matter. These are not just equipment trims on a C-Class sedan.
models.tradeoff: Think about doors, passenger space, roof operation, luggage and intended driving use. A sports-car role can be appealing while failing everyday passenger requirements. Do not assume similar-looking badges mean the same number of seats.
models.compare: Compare CLE Coupe and Cabriolet by roof and practicality. Compare an SL or AMG GT with the exact sports-car alternative and usage, not with a family SUV on a single prestige scale.
models.memory: CLE = coupe/cabriolet; SL = roadster; GT = ask which body
models.scenario: A friend says “AMG GT.” Ask whether they mean the sports coupe or the separately named four-door family before discussing the car.
models.power: Engine, drivetrain, seating and performance vary widely across these names. A dedicated Mercedes-AMG model is not equivalent to an AMG Line styling package on another car.

name: Lexus
intro: Lexus is a Japanese luxury brand associated with Toyota, with its own model families. IS and ES occupy different sedan roles; NX and RX are everyday SUV anchors; UX, TX, GX, LX and RZ add different sizes, utility roles and energy systems.
naming: h commonly identifies a hybrid, and a plus on specific hybrid names can identify a plug-in system. F SPORT equipment is not equivalent to a dedicated F model. Lexus model numbers are version names rather than a universal literal engine-displacement code.
warning: The course includes selected Canadian families plus explicitly labelled older/current road-recognition examples. Check the exact year, body, engine/drive configuration and current availability before using specifications or prices. The families below are selected for learning and recognition. Check the linked official range for current Canadian availability, model years, equipment and pricing. A familiar name may remain on used cars after new-car availability changes.

models.name: IS
models.explanation: IS is a Lexus sports-sedan family. It is different from ES, a separate sedan family, even though both names are short and both carry Lexus badges.
models.tradeoff: The IS belongs in a comparison for smaller lexus sedan. Check actual passenger fit, cargo access, exterior dimensions and the exact version’s running costs. Its category is a starting point, not a promise that it fits every person or task.
models.compare: Compare IS and ES on actual layout, comfort, passenger fit and powertrain. Do not assume alphabetical order gives a universal performance ranking.
models.scenario: A friend mentions a IS. Explain its role as smaller lexus sedan, then ask for the year, powertrain and equipment before comparing it with another Lexus.
models.power: IS versions have year-specific engine and drivetrain configurations. F SPORT equipment should not be treated as the same thing as a dedicated high-performance F product.

knowledgeCheck.prompt: Does F SPORT equipment make every Lexus a dedicated F performance model?

Only the badge colour differs
F SPORT means a plug-in battery

models.name: NX
